- [2023/05/28] Avery Palladio is serving as an architectural expert witness in the arbitration case Columbia Architects, LLP v. Warbucks Enterprises LLC.
- [2023/05/28] The case involves a dispute over architectural plans for a multistory structure in Tribeca, with Respondent Owner seeking damages exceeding $40 million.
- [2023/05/28] The issue is whether the inclusion of a 20th floor in the architectural plans violated the New York City Building Code, constituting a departure from the professional standard of care.
- [2023/05/28] Avery Palladio is licensed to practice architecture in New York and 46 other jurisdictions, including several countries and regions.
- [2023/05/28] Avery Palladio has served as principal design architect on over 1,000 projects and has testified as an expert witness in 36 judicial proceedings and arbitrations.
- [2023/05/28] The New York City Department of Buildings issued a stop-work order after the building topped out at 20 stories, citing non-compliance with building height regulations.
- [2023/05/28] The building height was compliant with the code during the Schematic Design Phase, but the code changed during the Design Development Phase.
- [2023/05/28] Phyllis Brunelleschi, representing the Architect, was assured by DOB representatives that the plans were compliant, which is central to the Architect's defense.
- [2023/05/28] The administrative appeal regarding the DOB's decision has not yet been decided.
- [2023/05/28] Avery Palladio's opinion is that the Architect's reliance on DOB representatives' assurances does not constitute a departure from the professional standard of care.
- [2023/05/28] Avery Palladio is compensated at $900 per hour for preparation and $10,000 per diem for appearing as a witness, with no contingency on the case outcome.
